findings.title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata lacks sender
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] to compare the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the installer. Sender is only set in build_integration when state contains sender, so legacy integrations or records created without a webhook have no sender key. Any reinstall attempt for such an installation raises KeyError and returns HTTP 500 instead of rendering github-integration-failed.html, blocking installation and exposing an internal error.

findings.title: OAuth token exchange failures raise 500 instead of install error
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen to exchange code for access_token and then get_user_info to fetch login outside any try/except. Network errors, timeouts, GitHub 4xx/5xx, or invalid/expired/reused code can raise instead of returning a payload without access_token. Only the parse_qsl body parsing is guarded, so those failures bubble up as HTTP 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page described in the PR.

findings.title: Fresh installations bypass installer identity check
findings.body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, without comparing pipeline github_authenticated_user to anything. Installation IDs are small sequential integers enumerable via the GitHub App API, so anyone who knows or guesses an installation_id can link another account's GitHub installation to their own Sentry organization if the webhook-created Integration row has not arrived yet, defeating the PR's stated goal of ensuring the completer is the installer.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer covers 404 handling
findings.body: test_installation_not_found stubs GET /app/installations/{id} with 404 but then drives the OAuth step with state ddd023... which does not match the pipeline signature 9cae5e... used elsewhere. OAuthLoginView therefore returns Invalid installation request on state mismatch before build_integration is ever reached. The 404 branch in build_integration that raises The GitHub installation could not be found is left unexercised, so regressions there will not be caught.
